reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and weekend adjustment helpers, but repeats the daily skip policy across next-date, upcoming-date and range calculations.

duplication.why: Daily exclusion logic is repeated across three consumers, and getNextDate duplicates its eligible-occurrence selection for forward and reverse searches.

placement.why: Holiday matching belongs in shared schedules, but server handlers also own recurrence policy that should reside alongside the shared date calculations.

scope.why: All changes directly support the requested daily skipping, range handler and holiday extensions.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must synchronize multiple policy implementations and independently maintained search bounds when extending nonworking-day handling.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getDatesInRange builds a parallel occurrence-processing path instead of sharing the recurrence policy implemented in getNextDate; getUpcomingDates independently repeats that policy.

disguised_duplication.where: The same daily exclusion decision appears as a find predicate in getNextDate, a negated filter in getUpcomingDates and an early null return in getDatesInRange.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains the holidays parameter; getNextDate adds daily-specific selection branches for forward and reverse searches, while getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange independently implement the daily exclusion policy.
